endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: (3) Static model / Dynamic retrieval corpus (e.g., retrieval-augmented generation architectures — the model is frozen but the data it reasons over changes, which requires corpus governance policies rather than model retraining governance).

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: The data powering the AI system must reflect current knowledge, necessitating continuous checks to determine the frequency of data updates for open clinical trials, treatment indications, guidelines, and biomarker-selection criteria.

endorsements.title: Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare (RUAIH) guidance
endorsements.issuer: The Joint Commission and Coalition for Health AI
endorsements.quote: Ensuring AI tools rely on up-to-date data.

endorsements.title: Utility of ChatGPT in Clinical Practice
endorsements.quote: Keeping ChatGPT’s training data up-to-date while ensuring data accuracy is crucial to address this limitation and enhance its use in clinical settings.

endorsements.title: Ethical Considerations of Using ChatGPT in Health Care
endorsements.quote: To address this, ChatGPT needs to undergo specific training and continuous updates tailored to the needs of clinical practice [ 73 ].

endorsements.title: Ethical Considerations and Fundamental Principles of Large Language Models in Medical Education: Viewpoint
endorsements.quote: These resources are to be updated regularly with the latest medical research, thereby reducing errors and biases as well as enhancing data credibility.

endorsements.title: A perspective for adapting generalist AI to specialized medical AI applications and their challenges
endorsements.quote: In practice, the efficacy of RAG relies on two aspects: (1) the quality of the external database, which should be high-quality and up-to-date 36 , 37 , and (2) the performance of the retrieval systems, which are responsible for identifying and extracting the most relevant content to supplement the LLM’s output 38 , 39 .

endorsements.title: Ethical Imperatives for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Clinical Nursing: Viewpoint on Responsible AI Use
endorsements.quote: Continuous monitoring should also include version control and scheduled updates of external data sources to prevent outdated or inconsistent information from influencing clinical recommendations [ 56 ].

endorsements.title: An auditable and source-verified framework for clinical AI decision support: integrating retrieval-augmented generation with data provenance
endorsements.quote: The knowledge base is not static; it is updated continuously as new evidence emerges.

evidence.title: EviLedger: governing clinical AI with a verifiable evidence ledger
evidence.outcome: Stale citations in LLM-based retrieval with versus without evidence ledger
evidence.quote: As an auditable memory layer for LLM-based retrieval, EviLedger reduces stale citations from 14.7% to 1.2% and unverifiable citations from 28.4% to 2.3%, while supporting p95 rollback in 5.13 s at 78M assertions.

evidence.title: An artificially intelligent, natural language processing chatbot designed to promote COVID-19 vaccination: A proof-of-concept pilot study
evidence.outcome: Chatbot accuracy in matching responses to user intents as COVID-19 information evolved
evidence.effect: Accuracy ranged from 54% to 91.1%; it lagged when new information emerged (e.g., Delta variant) and increased after new content was added.
evidence.quote: Accuracy lagged when new information related to COVID emerged, such as that related to the Delta variant.

evidence.title: Diagnostic Accuracy Masks Outdated Reasoning: Evaluating LLMs on Evolving Clinical Guidelines
evidence.outcome: Use of outdated (superseded) guideline vocabulary with a corpus containing superseded definitions
evidence.effect: Corpus containing superseded SIRS-based definitions increased superseded-vocabulary use in all four models relative to no context.
evidence.quote: First, injecting guideline context of any kind increased superseded-vocabulary use for every model relative to the no-context baseline.

evidence.title: ChatGPT and Patient Information in Nuclear Medicine: GPT-3.5 Versus GPT-4
evidence.outcome: Currency of ChatGPT-generated nuclear medicine patient information rated by expert assessors
evidence.effect: GPT-3.5 lacked accuracy and currency and omitted important information; GPT-4 was enhanced across appropriateness, accuracy, and currency despite some omissions.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT powered by GPT-3.5 provided patient information that was appropriate in terms of being patient-facing but lacked accuracy and currency and omitted important information.
evidence.sample_unit: patient information sheets (7 procedures x 2 models)

evidence.title: ChatGPT and mycosis- a new weapon in the knowledge battlefield
evidence.outcome: ChatGPT knowledge currency and accuracy in fungal infection scenario questions
evidence.effect: The authors report deficits in timely literature updates, individual advice, consistency, accuracy and data safety as the largest barriers, although most responses were judged compelling. No numbers were given.
evidence.quote: However, the largest barriers to implementation are deficits in indiviudal advice, timely literature updates, consistency, accuracy and data safety.

evidence.title: ChatGPT, alleato del farmacista clinico nella verifica delle herbal-drug interactions: potenzialità e limiti
evidence.outcome: Currency of ChatGPT knowledge for herbal-drug interaction checking
evidence.effect: Limitations include outdated data (last updated in January 2022) and lack of access to private databases.
evidence.quote: While ChatGPT proves useful for initial HDI screening, its limitations include outdated data (last updated in January 2022), lack of access to private databases, and occasional inaccuracies.

evidence.title: Patient Support in Obstructive Sleep Apnoea by a Large Language Model - ChatGPT 4o on Answering Frequently Asked Questions on First Line Positive Airway Pressure and Second Line Hypoglossal Nerve Stimulation Therapy: A Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: Medical adequacy and completeness of ChatGPT-4o answers on established (PAP) versus recent (HGNS) therapy
evidence.effect: Medical adequacy was higher for PAP (mean 4.9) than HGNS (mean 4.6, p<0.05). Completeness was confirmed in 45/51 ratings (88.24%) for PAP and 28/51 (54.9%) for HGNS.
evidence.quote: However, some substantial flaws regarding second line HGNS therapy are most likely due to recent advances in HGNS therapy and the consequent limited information available in LLM training data.

evidence.title: Annual updates of the European Association of Urology - European Society for Pediatric Urology (EAU-ESPU) paediatric urology guidelines: Are large-language models (LLM) better than the usual structured methodology?
evidence.effect: All three LLMs were unable to update guidelines with recent relevant literature because they lacked correct scientific database access.
evidence.quote: All three LLMs were unable to update the guidelines with the recent relevant literature because of the lack of access to the correct scientific databases.

evidence.title: Evaluating a Chatbot as a Companion for Patients With Breast Cancer: Collaborative Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: Outdated or incomplete guideline content in chatbot answers
evidence.effect: Incomplete answers omitted updates from recent therapeutic guidelines; 6 (5.8%) answers rated potentially harmful due to outdated or contextually inappropriate recommendations.
evidence.quote: In addition, 6 (5.8%) of the answers were rated as potentially harmful due to outdated or contextually inappropriate recommendations.
evidence.sample_unit: patient questions (chatbot responses rated by expert)

evidence.title: The Impact of Access to Clinical Guidelines on LLM-Based Treatment Recommendations for Chronic Hepatitis B
evidence.venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
evidence.outcome: Whether GPT-4 without context gave outdated guideline recommendations after guideline update
evidence.effect: Without context GPT-4 mostly adhered to the older 2015 WHO guidelines; only 51% of recommendations were coherent with the 2024 guidelines.
evidence.quote: Our findings showed that GPT-4, when enhanced with more context, aligns consistently with the latest WHO guidelines, whereas GPT-4 without additional context mostly adhered to the older 2015 WHO guidelines.

evidence.title: Accuracy of Large Language Model Responses Versus Internet Searches for Common Questions About Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy: Exploratory Simulation Study
evidence.outcome: Currency of LLM information on emerging GLP1RA concerns
evidence.effect: LLM lacked updated information on newly emerging concerns such as fertility and mental health, reflecting static training data limitations.
evidence.quote: However, it lacked updated information pertaining to newly emerging concerns surrounding GLP1RA use, such as the impact on fertility and mental health.

evidence.title: Updating CMV protocols in lung transplant patients: a single-center case study modeling use of generative AI for antimicrobial stewardship protocol development and economic impact analysis
evidence.outcome: Currency of evidence underlying AI-generated CMV prophylaxis protocol
evidence.effect: The AI-generated protocol was evidence-based without hallucination but relied on outdated evidence, with mean +$4740 per-patient cost (P < .01) versus guideline-based and institutional protocols.
evidence.quote: The AI-generated prophylaxis protocol was evidence-based without hallucination, but this conservative protocol relied on outdated evidence and was associated with significant increases in expected per-patient cost (mean +$4740, P < .01) compared to recent guideline-based and institutional protocols.
evidence.sample_unit: patients (aggregate cohort statistics used to generate simulated patients)

evidence.title: Accuracy, Usefulness, and Impact Variability of ChatGPT4o for COPD Medication Management: A Modified Delphi Study
evidence.outcome: Whether ChatGPT-4o COPD pharmacotherapy answers relied on current guidelines
evidence.effect: For one stable COPD pharmacotherapy question, all 3 simultaneous responses cited a retired clinical practice guideline, resulting in poor accuracy ratings.
evidence.quote: For one question on stable COPD pharmacotherapy, all 3 simultaneous responses cited a retired clinical practice guideline, resulting in poor accuracy ratings.
evidence.sample_unit: ChatGPT-4o responses (5 questions x 3 simultaneous responses)

evidence.title: Facts Fade Fast: Evaluating Memorization of Outdated Medical Knowledge in Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Obsolete pre-training knowledge leading to outdated recommendations
evidence.effect: All eight LLMs showed reliance on outdated knowledge; the study analyzes the influence of obsolete pre-training data and training strategies.
evidence.quote: Our evaluation of eight prominent LLMs on the datasets reveals consistent reliance on outdated knowledge across all models.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (MedChangeQA QA pairs where medical consensus changed; MedRevQA has 16,501)

evidence.title: Contradictions in Context: Challenges for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Healthcare
evidence.outcome: Effect of outdated or contradictory retrieved PubMed abstracts on RAG answer accuracy and consistency
evidence.effect: Contradictions between highly similar retrieved abstracts degraded performance, causing inconsistencies and reduced factual accuracy in model answers. No numbers are reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Our findings show that contradictions between highly similar abstracts do, in fact, degrade performance, leading to inconsistencies and reduced factual accuracy in model answers.

evidence.title: EviLedger: governing clinical AI with a verifiable evidence ledger
evidence.effect: Stale citations decreased from 14.7% to 1.2% with EviLedger; the abstract does not test a defined knowledge-source update schedule.
evidence.quote: As an auditable memory layer for LLM-based retrieval, EviLedger reduces stale citations from 14.7% to 1.2% and unverifiable citations from 28.4% to 2.3%, while supporting p95 rollback in 5.13 s at 78M assertions.

evidence.title: Improving accuracy of GPT-3/4 results on biomedical data using a retrieval-augmented language model
evidence.outcome: Outdated knowledge from training cutoff and incomplete retrieval corpus affecting answers
evidence.effect: RAG answer to glofitamab response rate question was inaccurate because the key trial paper was not in the corpus; GPT models trained only up to September 2021.
evidence.quote: The RAG model result was not accurate in answering this question because the official glofitamab trial efficacy paper [ 36 ] was not available on PubMed Central ( https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/ ) and therefore not included in the corpus.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 for Patient Education in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Radiotherapy: a Comparative Analysis
evidence.venue: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
evidence.outcome: Currency of evidence and guideline references in LLM responses
evidence.effect: Both models scored DISCERN 51-62 (good), but had deficiencies in evidence currency, guideline references, and long-term side effects.
evidence.quote: However, deficiencies were noted in the areas of evidence currency, guideline references, and long-term side effects.

commentary.bottom_line: One automated benchmark reports that an evidence ledger reduced stale citations from 14.7% to 1.2% across 3,200 guideline-change events, but it did not test a defined update schedule or documentation of cut-off dates. Seventeen studies show that outdated sources produce obsolete recommendations, so support for this practice rests on framework endorsement and indirect evidence.

perspectives.view: Only one study, a level 5 automated benchmark, tests a related intervention, and its abstract does not evaluate a scheduled update policy. Certainty is very low because the evidence is indirect, comes from a single study, and relies on benchmark design. The hazard studies show that stale content causes errors, but they do not show that scheduled updates prevent them.

In a German chatbot study, 6 of 104 answers (5.8%) were rated potentially harmful because of outdated or contextually inappropriate recommendations. A corpus containing superseded sepsis definitions increased superseded vocabulary in all four models tested. This suggests that an unmaintained retrieval corpus may introduce errors instead of preventing them.

A United States COVID-19 chatbot's intent-matching accuracy ranged from 54% to 91.1%. Accuracy lagged when new information emerged and rose after new content was added. A retrieval system answered a glofitamab question incorrectly because the key trial was missing from its corpus. These observations suggest that corpus currency affects output, although neither study tests a formal schedule.

An AI-generated CMV prophylaxis protocol relied on outdated evidence. In a simulation built from 165 patients, it cost a mean $4,740 more per patient (P < .01) than guideline-based and institutional protocols. No study reports the staffing or cost of maintaining a corpus on a schedule, so the return on that investment has not been measured.

Both CHAI frameworks list this practice as a must. The CHAI guide calls for continuous checks on how often data on trials, indications, guidelines, and biomarker criteria are updated. The CHAI playbook states that a retrieval corpus needs its own governance policy, separate from model retraining. These are consensus positions and have not been tested against outcomes.

The single test does not report the populations or care settings behind its guideline-change events. The only study involving limited English proficiency or non-English users documents the hazard and does not test the practice. Whether update schedules reduce obsolete advice for Medicaid, safety-net, or low-literacy patients is unknown.

In one study, all three ChatGPT-4o responses to a COPD pharmacotherapy question cited a retired guideline. Documented cut-off dates could help clinicians and patients judge how current an answer is. No study measures whether such disclosure affects trust or prompts people to seek a human.

commentary.research_gap: No study compares a defined corpus update schedule, or documentation of source databases and cut-off dates, against unmanaged corpora on clinical accuracy, patient outcomes, or cost. Prospective evaluations in deployed retrieval systems could measure stale-recommendation rates at different update intervals and record the staff time each interval requires.
commentary.underserved_note: The one test (epmc:PPR1157120) reports no information on Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. A German hazard study included limited English proficiency or non-English users but did not test the practice. The effect of scheduled updates in underserved populations is therefore unknown.
